pairs.subject: realtime-combat-semantics
pairs.evidence: src/types/combat-simulator.ts:38 CombatAbility gives area abilities only a radius, with no telegraph, lead-time or homing field, and the engine the route calls (simulation-engine.ts:371) resolves an AoE instantly on every living enemy, so the sim models the forbidden instant, untelegraphed, positional case and can never surface it.

techniques.evidence: src/types/combat-simulator.ts:38 Area abilities carry a radius and nothing else: no lead time, no cue, no homing flag. The engine ignores the radius and hits every living enemy at once.

src/lib/combat/simulation-engine.ts:368 Dodge is a flat invulnerability duration (default 0.5 s) that an RNG/low-HP rule picks. It has no trigger window relative to the incoming hit and no stat-scaled magnitude, so both axes are collapsed. (The engine sits outside the context's file list, but the context's route calls it directly.)

src/types/combat-simulator.ts:32 Every time value is typed in seconds and named by its kind (cooldownSec, castTimeSec, durationSec, attackIntervalSec, stun duration in seconds). There is no tick period to confuse with a cooldown. Escape windows are not modelled, because there are no regions.

Yet ForgedAbility's stats/comboEntry schema and the GAS_RULES in src/lib/prompts/ability-forge.ts carry no telegraph, lead-time or homing requirement, so generated AoE abilities are never asked to owe the player a cue.

techniques.evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/forge/constants.ts:14 Area abilities are a first-class forge output, but neither the output schema nor the prompt rules mention a telegraph or lead time (searched for 'telegraph', 'lead time' and 'period' in the prompt builder: no hits).

src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/forge/ability-diff.ts:22 Cooldown, anim duration, damage start/end and recovery are each typed with a unit and kept in separate groups. The prompt also enforces the 0.4-1.5 s wind-up and 0.1-0.5 s recovery bands. Caveat: the schema has no tick-period field for lingering effects such as the 'fire patch'.

src/lib/prompts/ability-forge.ts:272 The forge's own prompt builder makes the dead tag a mandatory member of the activation-blocked set for every generated ability. That is technique step 2 verbatim. ForgeResult.tsx:127 renders the blocked tags.
